questions.question: Explain African nationalism and Pan-Africanism and how events in Africa influenced the Africanists.
questions.expected_answer: African nationalism: pride, self-reliance, Africans lead own struggle; Lembede (Youth League 1944, died 1947), wary of alliances and communism; Africanists. Pan-Africanism: unity of people of African descent; Du Bois, Garvey, Pan-African Congresses; anti-colonial after WWII. Ghana independent 1957 (Nkrumah); All-African People's Conference Accra December 1958; 1960 Year of Africa (17 countries). Showed freedom possible soon.

questions.question: Explain why the Africanists broke away from the ANC.
questions.expected_answer: Strongest in Transvaal (Orlando), journal The Africanist. Objections: Freedom Charter's "belongs to all, black and white" accepted conquest; Congress Alliance multiracial, minorities given equal weight; communist influence (COD) and foreign ideology; ANC too cautious, poorly organised, paralysed by Treason Trial. ANC (Luthuli, Tambo, Mandela) defended non-racialism. Break at Transvaal conference November 1958.

questions.question: Describe the formation, aims and plans of the PAC and the role of Robert Sobukwe.
questions.expected_answer: Founded 4-6 April 1959, Orlando Communal Hall; 6 April = Van Riebeeck anniversary; Sobukwe president, Leballo secretary. Aims: unite Africans in African nationalism, overthrow white domination, government of Africans by Africans for Africans, united states of Africa; African = loyalty to Africa and accept majority rule; one human race. Slogans Izwe Lethu, Africa for the Africans; flag with Africa map and star over Ghana. Strong in Vereeniging area (Sharpeville, Evaton) and Western Cape (Langa, Nyanga); claimed tens of thousands of members. Sobukwe: born Graaff-Reinet 1924, Healdtown, Fort Hare (SRC president 1949), teacher, Wits lecturer in African languages ("Prof"), gentle, principled. Freedom by 1963; status campaign 1959; anti-pass campaign for 21 March 1960 (before ANC's 31 March); leave passes, go to police stations; "no bail, no defence, no fine"; non-violence; debate about preparation and rivalry.
